deep.reconstruction:
This page is the start of a 'Préliminaires' section. It recalls Hilbert-space facts needed for a study of singular values (s-numbers) of compact operators. The context is Grothendieck's 1953 work on eigenvalue distribution and Schatten-type classes of nuclear and Fredholm operators, which fed into Produits tensoriels topologiques and 'La théorie de Fredholm'.

(0) Crossed-out box at the top. It refers to an earlier inequality (31), presumably a Hölder-type inequality for singular values with exponents p, q, s and 1/s = 1/p + 1/q. He proposes letting p → ∞ and q → 0 to obtain, in the limit, an inequality on the individual ρ_i(u). This is the standard device of passing from ℓ^s-type inequalities to pointwise or multiplicative ones, such as Weyl/Horn products or Ky Fan inequalities. The passage was abandoned and replaced by the elementary preliminaries below.

(1) The conjugate space Ē. If E is Hilbert, Ē is Hilbert and E' ≅ Ē (Riesz).

(2) Approximation property of Hilbert spaces. Consequently, compact operators are norm limits of finite-rank operators, and E' ⊗̂ F → L(E,F) is injective (its image is the trace class).

(3) Adjoint u*: F → E and the C*-identity ‖u*u‖ = ‖u‖².

(4) Spectral theorem for a compact hermitian u: u = Σ λ_i ē_i ⊗ e_i, i.e. x ↦ Σ λ_i (x|e_i) e_i. Here λ_i → 0, the λ_i are real, and u ≥ 0 iff all λ_i ≥ 0. Consequence: the square root of a compact positive operator.

(5) Polar decomposition of a general compact u: E → F. Set |u| = √(u*u), a positive operator, with ‖|u|x‖ = ‖ux‖. Hence ux = U|u|x, where U is isometric on the closure of |u|(E) (and 0 on its complement). Dually, |u| = Vu with V: F → E isometric on the closure of u(E); in fact V = U*. This gives (***): u = U|u|, |u| = Vu, ‖U‖, ‖V‖ ≤ 1, and in particular ‖u‖ = ‖|u|‖.

(6) Schmidt decomposition. From |u| = Σ ρ_i ē_i ⊗ e_i with ρ_i ≥ 0, one gets (****): u = Σ ρ_i ē_i ⊗ f_i, where f_i = U e_i is orthonormal. Conversely, any such decomposition gives |u| = Σ ρ_i ē_i ⊗ e_i, so the ρ_i are the eigenvalues of |u| and the e_i are its eigenvectors. Also u* = Σ ρ_i f̄_i ⊗ e_i, so |u*| has the same nonzero eigenvalues as |u|.

The next page defines ρ_n(u) = λ_n(|u|), proves the Courant–Fischer minimax characterization and ρ_n(uv) ≤ ‖u‖ρ_n(v), and states the Ky Fan inequalities.
errors: The transcription's hermitian decomposition 'u = Σ ρ_i ē_i⊗e_i, où λ_i→0' should read u = Σ λ_i ē_i⊗e_i; the image shows the same symbol as in λ_i → 0.
Minor gap: in (****) the f_i = U e_i are orthonormal only for indices with ρ_i > 0, since U is isometric only on the closure of the range of |u|. Harmless, because the other terms vanish.
V is not identified as U* on this page. That is not wrong, just not stated.

deep.surprise_reason: Textbook preliminaries (Riesz, C*-identity, spectral theorem, polar and Schmidt decompositions) written up for a singular-value study. The only non-routine element is an abandoned limit argument whose content is not recoverable and is covered by known Ky Fan/Horn results.
